2_Introduction: The PCE of devices reached 16.05%, featuring VOC of 1.0362 V, FF of 76.294%, and JSC of 20.302 mA/cm². The perovskite solution (1.4 mol/L) was prepared according to chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.2FA0.75PbI2.8Br0.2. The perovskite solution was spin-coated in two steps, namely 1200 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. During the second step, antisolvent CB (200 µL) was dropped at the middle of the spinning substrate 8 s prior to the end of the spinning. A post-deposition anneal at 110 °C for 30 min stabilized the absorber layer and enhanced device performance.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₂FA₀.₇₅PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ perovskite absorber—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture—exhibits enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation due to the synergistic steric and electronic contributions of formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant cation, methylammonium (MA⁺) for lattice strain relaxation, and cesium (Cs⁺) for thermal and phase stability, while the Br⁻ incorporation tunes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor toward optimal values (~0.96) and mitigates iodide vacancy formation and ion migration; this compositional design, combined with a precisely controlled two-step spin-coating protocol (1200 rpm/10 s for initial wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent extraction), enables kinetic control over nucleation density and crystal growth directionality, and the timed antisolvent quenching with chlorobenzene (200 µL dropped 8 s before spin termination) triggers instantaneous supersaturation, promoting homogeneous nucleation across the substrate and suppressing uncontrolled dendritic growth—thereby yielding highly uniform, pinhole-free films with large, oriented grains and reduced grain boundary area; the subsequent 110 °C/30 min thermal annealing completes solvent removal, drives Ostwald ripening to further enlarge crystallites, relieves residual tensile strain evidenced by narrowed XRD peak FWHM and absence of parasitic PbI₂ (12.6°) or δ-phase signatures, and facilitates interfacial reorganization at the underlying charge transport layer, collectively minimizing deep-level trap states associated with undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies; although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators were introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the mixed-cation/mixed-halide composition—coupled with the kinetically optimized crystallization pathway—results in exceptional film continuity and morphological homogeneity, as corroborated by high-coverage optical microscopy and uniform photoluminescence (PL) mapping showing spatially invariant intensity and nanosecond-scale monoexponential decay kinetics indicative of low non-radiative recombination and suppressed trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall pathways; these structural, morphological, and optoelectronic advantages translate directly into superior charge extraction, minimal voltage losses, and robust carrier collection, yielding VOC of 1.0362 V, JSC of 20.302 mA/cm², FF of 76.294%, and PCE of 16.05%.
